text:
Patrick Kane came back to Chicago this season, the place where he won three Stanley Cups, a Conn Smythe, a Hart and an Art Ross, and the reunion has been more setup than finish. He has one goal in 17 games, none in his last 16, on 4.0 expected goals over that stretch. He missed time on injured reserve before being activated on November 12, and his minutes have slipped to 16.7 a night over his last ten.

The playmaking is still there: 7 assists in those ten games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 95th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. The finishing will likely come back some way; at 37, shooting 3.1% is well below anything he's done.

The worry is the other end. With Kane on at five on five, Chicago has had only 38.44% of the expected goals, and the team has also scored 8.15 fewer goals than expected with him out there, so luck is hurting both ways. Watch whether he lands back next to Connor Bedard; The Athletic's Mark Lazerus reported it sounded unlikely on his return.
headline: Patrick Kane, home again, waits on a goal
